subject: research/accel-cascade
professional: a keyword-spotting / TinyML systems researcher (the kind who referees for tinyML or DAC/ISLPED) with a statistician's eye for selection bias. First checks: that the selection among ~41,000 cascades on validation does not leak into test, that the 75% accuracy baseline is representative of KWS practice, and that classifier-only energy is a meaningful system metric.

evidence.correctness: Could not retrain (needs the 2.4 GB Speech Commands tarball, not fetched), so recomputed from the shipped experiments/results.json with a fresh script: per-target mean single/any energy, test accuracy, cascades-picked counts, per-seed ratios and test-accuracy differences all match the README table and results.txt exactly (e.g. 0.72: 8.66 vs 6.18 nJ, ratio 0.87/0.71/0.63/0.64/0.78, 5 of 5). Re-ran experiments/gap.py: gap.txt regenerated byte-identical (git status clean). Recomputed accel_kws cost.energy_per_inference_nj(5184, 4) = 10.86 nJ and 10368 MACs = 21.72 nJ, matching the stored e_nj. Best single test accuracy 0.752 to 0.758 over seeds, matching 0.755. Check was of the stored numbers and the cost arithmetic, not of the training, so not 4.
evidence.completeness: README claims checked: speaker-disjoint splits (results.json data.speaker_overlap all 0, present); 40 models x 5 seeds (designs lists present); ~41,000 cascades per seed (n_cascades present); table, gap.txt, winner's-curse check, 6 tests, all scripts present. The 'Does it matter' front-end argument is only cited from accel-frontend, not computed here. Next-steps items (silence class, early exit) are honestly listed as not done. No stubs.
evidence.verification: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests: 6 tests OK. Mutation 1: margin top-2 index changed to top-3 in cascade.margin, a test failed (caught). Mutation 2: in cascade.run changed `margin(lg1) < t` to `<= t`: all 6 tests still passed (SURVIVED). That boundary matters in practice because thresholds are quantiles of integer margins, so ties at the threshold are common. Nothing tests experiments/run.py (pick, candidates, selection on validation only) or the energy/escalation accounting end to end; the selection-on-validation guarantee, the central methodological claim, is untested.
evidence.craft: Read src/accel_cascade/cascade.py, tests/test_cascade.py, experiments/run.py, gap.py. Small and clear, docstrings state the contract, validation-only selection is explicit in code. Defects: cascade.pareto is never used by any experiment; run.py has a dead loop `for c in cands: pass` with a stale comment; candidates() is O(40*40*58) Python-level calls re-sorting margins each time (17 min run) rather than caching margin(lg1) per small model; sys.path hacks import accel-kws; cascade.run recomputes margin per threshold.
evidence.claims: Checked: table numbers (match results.json); 'validation about 0.03 above test' (gap.txt 0.023 to 0.041, ok); 'best single 0.755 (35 to 47 nJ)' (ok); 'about 50 times the classifier' and 'MFCC 54 times' cited from accel-frontend, not re-derived and flagged as assumed constants. Headline 'cut energy by 0 to 28%' is the seed-mean ratio at the best target; the per-seed saving reaches 37% (ratio 0.625) so the range understates the spread, and at 0.70 one seed has ratio 1.003. 'Constants match Horowitz within 4%' rests on accel-horowitzcheck, while accel-kws/cost.py says its constants were typed from memory; both stated. Limits and 'simulation only' disclosure are present. The 'No CU Boulder group is built on' sentence is a template artefact.
evidence.fitness: Nearest prior work: early-exit / cascaded KWS (e.g. two-stage always-on wake models, Viola-Jones style cascades, BranchyNet, Sun et al. and Gruenstein/Google small-footprint KWS cascades, Hello Edge Zhang 2017). The README cites only Viola and Jones and Warden, so related work is thin. The result (small, negative-ish: classifier-only saving is dwarfed by front end) is sound for its setup, honestly reported with a winner's-curse check, and a researcher could rerun it from the documented commands. Novelty is modest: the margin-gated cascade on a 1-hidden-layer MLP is a known construct and the contribution is the front-end-dominance quantification.
evidence.domain: A KWS/TinyML practitioner would object that: the models are one-hidden-layer MLPs at ~75% accuracy on an 11-class subsample, far from DS-CNN/MLPerf Tiny (~90%+ on 12 classes), so cascade gains on a weak baseline may not transfer; always-on KWS is dominated by silence/noise, which is precisely the regime where cascades pay and it is not measured; energy is MAC-count only (no control, leakage, SRAM for the second model, wake-up latency); no measured silicon. Method choices (validation-only selection, 5 seeds, test SE quoted) are good statistical practice. Departure is in scope, not in rigor.

defects.what: Mutation `margin < t` to `<= t` in the core escalation rule passes all tests; thresholds are quantiles of integer margins so ties are real, and no test covers the validation-only selection in run.py
Headline range '0 to 28%' is the seed-mean; per-seed savings reach 37% and one seed shows +0.3% energy, so the stated range is neither a per-seed nor a confidence range
Isolated-word clips and weak MLP baseline: the regime where always-on cascades matter (silence) is unmeasured, so the conclusion 'cosmetic' is conditional on the front-end constants and the benchmark
Dead code: unused cascade.pareto and a no-op `for c in cands: pass` loop with stale comment
Related-work section cites only Viola-Jones; early-exit/two-stage KWS literature absent

verdict: A small, honest, reproducible-from-stored-results negative result: every number in the README table matches results.json and gap.py regenerates byte-identically, selection is validation-only with a winner's-curse check, and limits are stated. It does not meet the bar because verification scores 2: a boundary mutation in the core escalation rule survived all 6 tests and the experiment pipeline is untested. The training was not re-run (dataset not fetched), related work is thin, and the weak MLP baseline with classifier-only energy keeps domain at 2. Finished (completeness 3) but not at senior-professional level overall.
